lines:
Responsibilities: Builds replaceable read models for Chat lists, semantic timelines, evidence lookup, full-text search, artifact/error/extension joins, and portable-session discovery. It accelerates inspection but never becomes evidence authority.
Owned records/files: disposable chat_summary, timeline_projection, evidence_locator, FTS/token indexes, source_cursor, projection_schema_version, and rebuild_health tables. Every row carries source kind (LocalSqlite or PortableProject), ChatId, canonical cursor/hash, and projection version; portable rows are explicitly marked noncanonical.
Keys and ordering: local timelines follow committed (ChatId, BranchId, sequence); portable timelines follow verified parent-linked segment and event order. Timestamps never merge concurrent portable branches. Projection row IDs derive from stable source IDs so applying a committed item twice is idempotent.
Ports: exposes read-only paginated ProjectionReadPort/SearchPort to the core Desktop API and ProjectionMaintenancePort to the storage coordinator. It consumes committed projection outbox cursors, reads LocalHistoryReadPort, reads verified portable segments through PortableHistoryReadPort, and resolves only metadata/pages from artifact, capture, and log stores.
Durability/degraded behavior: projection writes are independent of canonical commit and may lag. Gaps, schema changes, checksum failures, or corruption mark results stale/catching-up, drop the affected projection, and rebuild from canonical sources; no projection value is used to infer missing canonical state. Portable source disappearance removes only its cache rows.
Retention/performance: indexes obey configurable disk/FTS quotas and source visibility, use incremental batches and cancellable rebuilds, and may be evicted wholesale. Indexed list/search queries target p95 under 100 ms for 100k semantic events; expensive evidence is lazy and cursor-paginated. Backpressure slows projection catch-up, never canonical commits.
Security/non-responsibilities: indexes contain only already-redacted semantic/searchable fields and opaque credential references; secrets, raw lease material, and unredacted debug payloads are excluded. This module cannot write local or portable history, acknowledge capability effects, edit JSON, activate repairs/extensions, or authorize replay.

data.name: Disposable Query Projections, Search & Indexes
data.technology: Rust projection workers over disposable SQLite/FTS indexes
